metaDescription: Five generators with a 30 amp outlet compared by receptacle type (TT-30R, L5-30R, L14-30R), running watts, fuel and CO protection for RVs and home backup.
expertTake: The Westinghouse 4650 with 3600 running watts is the pick for most trailers, because it carries both RV style 30 amp receptacles on one panel. The Westinghouse 6500 dual fuel is the choice for anyone who also wants a transfer switch connection at home. Skip this category if you want 50 amp service for a big coach, because every machine here stops well short of what that panel can ask for.
introParagraphs: The phrase thirty amp generator hides three different plugs that do not fit each other. One is the flat bladed receptacle a travel trailer's shore cord uses, one is a locking cousin of it with the same capacity, and the third is a four prong receptacle that feeds a home transfer switch at a higher voltage. Buying the wrong one means an adapter or a dead end.

This guide sorts machines by the receptacles actually on the panel and the running power behind them. It leaves out cords, inlet boxes and adapters, since those are accessories, and concentrates on the generators that you plug them into.

products.name: Westinghouse 4650W peak, 3600W running generator, 4 gal tank
products.description:
Two different 30 amp receptacles on one panel is the reason this Westinghouse leads: a TT-30R, the flat bladed RV plug, and an L5-30R twist lock. Beside them sit two 5-20R household duplex outlets. At 3600 running watts the 30 amp circuit is exactly saturated, since 30 amps at 120 volts is about 3600 watts.

The 4 gallon tank has a fuel gauge, and the listing claims up to 14 hours of run time per fill at a light load. A CO sensor is fitted, and the machine ships with oil, a funnel, a tool kit and a manual, so it can run the day it arrives. It is a conventional open frame generator with a recoil start only, which means a cold start takes a firm pull and the waveform is rougher than an inverter's.

What you gain over an inverter at this size is simplicity and cost, and what you give up is quiet and electronic friendliness. A surge protector on the coach inlet is sensible. It is a straightforward machine that a local shop can repair, and the brand's service reach is wide. Because the machine is a plain open frame design, an owner who wants electronics protection should plug the coach into it through a surge protector, and keep the exhaust pointed away from the awning. In year three the usual jobs are a fresh plug, a clean air filter and fuel that has not turned to varnish.
products.bestFor: Travel trailer owners who want both RV style 30 amp plugs on one panel.
pros: TT-30R and L5-30R on the same panel
3600 running watts matches the 30 amp ceiling
CO sensor and a ready to run kit with oil

products.badge: Best Dual Fuel at This Size
products.name: Westinghouse 4650W peak dual fuel generator, 3600W gas, 3240W propane
products.description:
The dual fuel sibling keeps the same panel and tank and adds propane at 3240 rated watts, a loss of 360 watts or 10 percent, with peak held at 4650 on both fuels. Because the peak does not fall, a stubborn compressor starts as easily on propane as on gasoline. The panel has one 5-20R household duplex plus the TT-30R and L5-30R.

For a camper who wants to carry a propane cylinder rather than a gasoline can, this model is the simplest answer. A CO sensor comes standard, and a 4 gallon tank with gauge is generous. At 3240 watts on propane the 30 amp circuit is not quite saturated, which means appliances that run near its limit have a little more margin.

Expect a propane hose to be part of the kit, and plan on an annual soapy water check of the joints. Gasoline in the tank still needs stabilizer if the generator sits. Switching fuels is done at the panel, and the machine should be run until the carburetor is empty of gasoline before a long propane stay, so that a stale bowl does not cause a hard start later. A spare propane hose is cheap insurance. If you rarely use propane, the cheaper single fuel model is the better buy, since the extra regulator and hose are parts you will maintain without using.
products.bestFor: Campers who want to run from a propane cylinder with the same RV plugs.
pros: TT-30R and L5-30R plus a household duplex
cons: Propane output falls to 3240 rated watts

products.name: Westinghouse 6500W peak dual fuel generator, 5300W gas running
products.description:
This model adds a transfer switch ready outlet to the RV style TT-30R, which means one machine can feed a trailer on the road and a home panel in an outage. It rates 5300 running and 6500 peak watts on gasoline, and 4800 running and 5800 peak on propane. A 4.7 gallon tank gives it longer runs than the smaller models.

The kit includes oil, a funnel, a propane hose, a tool kit and a wheel kit, which you will need because it is a large conventional machine. The TT-30R carries only about 3600 watts of the 5300, so the remaining watts reach the house through the transfer outlet. That is the point of the design: the generator's output is larger than any single 30 amp plug.

For home backup the transfer switch connection should be installed by an electrician with an interlock or a proper switch. Propane costs 500 rated watts but stores for years. If one generator has to serve a trailer and a house, this is the sensible choice. Because the machine is large, measure the garage door and the truck bed before you commit, and plan where it will sit during an outage, outside and well away from any window. A fully fueled 4.7 gallon tank adds real weight, so move it empty if you can.
products.bestFor: Owners who want one generator for a trailer and for home backup.
pros: TT-30R plus a transfer switch ready outlet
Propane hose and wheel kit included

products.badge: Best Inverter with RV Ready Outlet
products.name: WEN 6800W surge, 5100W rated dual fuel inverter generator
products.description:
Inverter output is what separates this WEN from the Westinghouse machines: clean power for modern electronics from a 224cc dual fuel engine, with 5100 rated watts on gasoline and 6800 at surge. It is described as RV ready, and a bonded neutral 240 volt configuration supports slow Level 2 charging of an electric vehicle. An automatic CO Watchdog shuts the engine down when exhaust gas builds up.

The listing does not itemize the receptacle type in the excerpt, so confirm that the 30 amp outlet is the TT-30R or L5-30R your cord needs. On propane the unit holds 4500 rated and 6000 surge, a loss of 600 watts. Electric start and a fuel shutoff valve make it a convenient machine to live with.

It costs more than the conventional units because of the inverter electronics, and what you buy is quiet and clean power. For a modern coach with sensitive boards it is a better match than a plain generator. Because the output exceeds a single 30 amp plug, ask which outlets carry the remaining watts, and whether a 240 volt inlet is part of the panel before you rely on it for a home connection.
products.bestFor: Owners who want clean inverter power, CO shutdown and an RV ready outlet.
pros: Electric start with fuel shutoff valve
cons: Receptacle type not itemized in the excerpt

products.name: RVMP Flex Power 3300W peak, 2700W continuous inverter generator
products.description:
Engineered by a team that builds RV power systems, according to its maker, this is the smallest machine in the group and the only one built as a compact inverter. It outputs true sine wave power at 2700 continuous and 3300 peak watts, with an automatic CO shutoff and a 30 amp ready connection.

At 2700 watts it does not saturate the 30 amp circuit, which tops out near 3600, so it will carry one air conditioner and the essentials but not the microwave alongside. That is the honest tradeoff: a small, quiet, RV oriented machine with a 30 amp plug that it cannot fully use.

Compared with the Westinghouse 4650 it gives up 900 running watts and the dual receptacle variety, but gains the inverter waveform and a lighter case. If your rig has one air conditioner and you value quiet, it is a reasonable choice. Check the warranty path, since the brand is newer. Because the machine will not fill the 30 amp circuit, it is best understood as a quiet single air conditioner generator that happens to have the right plug, not as a way to power a fully loaded trailer.
products.bestFor: Small trailers with one air conditioner that want quiet and a 30 amp plug.
cons: 2700 continuous leaves the 30 amp circuit unused
Newer brand with a short record

buyingCriteria.explanation: A TT-30R is the flat bladed plug of a trailer's shore cord, an L5-30R is a locking 120 volt plug, and an L14-30R is a four prong 120/240 volt plug for transfer switches. The Westinghouse 4650 lists both of the first two, and the 6500 adds a transfer switch outlet. Match the receptacle to your cord before you shop. A mismatched plug usually tempts buyers into a cheap adapter, which adds one more connection that can heat under load.

A 30 amp, 120 volt receptacle carries about 3600 watts. The Westinghouse 4650 at 3600 running exactly fills it, while the 6500 and the WEN at 5100 exceed any single plug. Extra output reaches loads through other outlets or a 240 volt connection. Always keep the combined load on the shore cord under about 80 percent of that ceiling for a safety margin.

The Westinghouse machines are conventional and cost less per watt, while the WEN and RVMP are inverters with cleaner power. A modern coach's converter and electronics prefer the inverter. A conventional unit needs a surge protector at the inlet.

The Westinghouse 4650 dual fuel loses 360 watts on propane, the 6500 loses 500 and the WEN 600. A smaller loss helps boondocking on a cylinder. Do your load math on the propane figure. If you can only store one fuel, choose the unit whose propane loss you can live with.

The Westinghouse 4650 and 6500 list a CO sensor. The WEN and RVMP list automatic shutoffs. A sensor is not a placement rule, so keep the generator 20 feet from windows. A battery powered CO alarm inside the trailer is the cheapest extra layer of protection.
Only the Westinghouse 6500 lists a transfer switch ready outlet. A home connection should use a proper inlet and interlock installed by an electrician. Never backfeed through a household outlet.

specDecoder.meaning: A 120 volt, 30 amp receptacle with flat blades, used by travel trailers. It carries about 3600 watts, which is why the plug is the natural ceiling for a trailer's shore connection.
specDecoder.watchFor: Both Westinghouse 4650 models and the 6500 list one.

specDecoder.meaning: A 120 volt, 30 amp locking receptacle with curved blades. It resists being pulled out.
A four prong 120/240 volt receptacle to feed a home transfer switch or inlet box.
Continuous output that the machine holds for hours.
specDecoder.watchFor: Rated figures here run from 2700 to 5300, and only the 3600 watt machine matches the circuit it feeds.

specDecoder.meaning: A wiring option that allows some 240 volt loads such as EV charging.

howWeEvaluated.title: Receptacle fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at which 30 amp receptacles each panel lists. The Westinghouse 4650 has two types and the 6500 adds a transfer outlet. Missing details counted against units.

howWeEvaluated.title: Running output
howWeEvaluated.description: We ranked on rated watts: 5300 on the Westinghouse 6500, 5100 on the WEN, 3600 on the 4650 and 2700 on the RVMP. We noted which exceed the 3600 watt circuit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fuel behavior
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared propane losses. The Westinghouse 4650 loses 360 watts, the 6500 loses 500 and the WEN 600. Smaller losses ranked higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated CO sensors from automatic shutoffs. The WEN and RVMP list shutoffs. Placement was treated as the first safeguard.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed parts reach and the supplied kit. Westinghouse ships oil, a funnel and tools, which saves a first day trip to the store. Figures come from manufacturers' listings, not our measurements.

cards.label: Conventional
cards.text: The Westinghouse machines cost less per watt and are easy to repair. They are louder and need a surge protector.

cards.label: Inverter
cards.text: The WEN and RVMP give clean power and lower noise. They cost more per watt.

howToChoose.note: Choose conventional for cost and inverter for parks and electronics.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: The same receptacle as your shore cord, running watts near 3600 and a CO safeguard. Do not buy an adapter if a direct plug exists. Check the cord's rating and gauge too: a 30 amp cord that is too long and too thin drops voltage and runs warm under an air conditioner load.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Westinghouse 4650 has the TT-30R and L5-30R. The RVMP is the compact choice for one air conditioner. Its recoil start and plain waveform are the compromises, and a surge protector at the inlet covers the second.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want home backup as well. The Westinghouse 6500 gives both connections.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only need a trailer plug. The Westinghouse 4650 does it.

maintenance.why: Conventional engines burn some oil. Low oil shutdown ends a night early.
Dual fuel models use hoses. Soapy water shows leaks.
Corroded blades heat under load and can melt the plug body. Clean contacts with a brush and replace a plug that is discolored.
Dust clogs the element and fouls the plug.
A 4 gallon tank of old gasoline gums the carburetor. Stabilize or drain.

faq.q: What does a 30 amp generator mean?
faq.a: It has at least one 30 amp receptacle, which carries about 3600 watts at 120 volts. The plug type varies between flat blade, locking and four prong versions, so the label alone does not tell you whether it fits your cord.

faq.q: Which plug does my trailer need?
faq.a: Most trailers use a flat blade TT-30P shore cord, which needs a TT-30R receptacle. A locking L5-30 plug needs the matching locking receptacle, and the Westinghouse 4650 models list both.
Only through a transfer switch or an interlock installed by an electrician. The Westinghouse 6500 lists a transfer switch ready outlet, and the right inlet box and cord complete the connection.

faq.q: Is a 30 amp unit enough for two air conditioners?
faq.a: No. Two compressors starting together exceed 3600 watts, and a 30 amp plug cannot carry more than that anyway. You need a larger machine and a 50 amp connection for two air conditioners.
Not in these listings, and cords are a separate purchase. Buy a cord that matches the receptacle and has a heavy enough gauge for the length, since a long thin cord drops voltage and heats up.
Inverter for quiet and clean power on a modern coach, conventional for cost and easy repairs. Most RV parks prefer inverter machines, and conventional units need a surge protector for electronics.
